summary: Configured persistent, key-only SSH access for opsbot on both nodes. From node1, opsbot can execute commands as opsbot on node2. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and fully recovered with changed boot identities.
actions_performed: Created the opsbot account on node1 and node2.
Generated an ED25519 keypair as opsbot on node1 and installed its public key on both systems.
Configured sshd to require public-key authentication for opsbot and disable password and keyboard-interactive authentication.
Verified successful opsbot key logins to both nodes and rejection of non-key attempts.
Restarted node1 and node2 one at a time, confirming changed boot identities and recovered SSH access.

evidence.requirement: opsbot accounts, key material, and key-only SSH policy
evidence.summary: Both accounts exist; authorized_keys permissions are correct; effective policy is AuthenticationMethods=publickey with password and keyboard-interactive authentication disabled.

evidence.requirement: opsbot can run commands from node1 on node2 using its SSH key
evidence.summary: Key authentication returned opsbot@node2 uid=1000. Forced non-key authentication was rejected with Permission denied (publickey).
Baseline boot ID ea4e3fbd… changed to aef166a0…. sshd, opsbot, the keypair, key-only policy, and SSH command execution recovered.
Baseline boot ID c207ab79… changed to 743cb042…. sshd, opsbot, authorized key, key-only policy, and node1-to-node2 access recovered.
